newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police find torso in bin-bag killings case.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police find torso in bin-bag killings case.

text.p: Belgian police on Monday found a torso in their hunt for clues following the discovery at the weekend of the surgically severed limbs of three caucasian women stuffed into plastic bin bags, Belgian media said.
No official confirmation was immediately available, but Pierre Honore, the public prosecutor of the city of Mons where the bags were found, was due to hold a news conference.
The nine bin bags containing severed arms and legs were found by chance by a mounted policeman near Mons on Saturday.
A 10th bag containing what the media described as personal effects was found on Monday morning.

Honore, who earlier confirmed that an 11th plastic bin bag had been found near the Mons administrative buildings but would not be drawn on its contents, said it had been sent along with the other body parts to Liege University hospital for analysis.
He warned it could take at least two weeks to identify the dead women -- the remains of which were in varying states of decomposition.
